sourceInformation.source: Yars' Revenge (Atari, 1982), designed by Howard Scott Warshaw; an original, unaffiliated tribute.
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed overhead x/y arena with dimensional pixel-art relief and decorative z height
sourceInformation.tech: Plain JavaScript, Canvas 2D and Web Audio; my-3D2dge 0.89.1 at 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691 with one boot-flag fix; AI Hub protocol 1, client 1.4.0 at 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869. Dependency-free Node build; single offline HTML.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original articulated insect bodies, cellular fortresses, cosmic ruins, shaded pixel materials, emissive rails, static and layered destruction; native engine primitives, actors, shapes and lights. No external images or fonts.
sourceInformation.animation: Native update/draw procedural posing with segmented abdomen, six legs, four wings, antennae, biting, banking, charge, recoil effects, respawn, transforming heart, moving shields and surviving swarm.
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-only electrical drones, pulse/glass motifs across three sectors, oscillator/noise effects and synthesized formant gibberish voices with captions. Engine music/sfx/voice buses, first-run music 10%, saved settings respected. No recorded audio or text-to-speech.
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and simultaneous local 1-2 co-op. AI Hub shared-world online 1-2 co-op with authoritative host, quantized actions, acknowledged siege edges, full-state recovery, local prediction, remote interpolation and a host with no player avatar. The hub supplies remote sessions; standalone has no matchmaking.
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted automated testing. Unified npm test covers fixed-step rules, ordinary-action solo/Assist/co-op campaigns, final recovery, deterministic replay, drawn/undrawn state, packaged file:// play, native menus/rebinding, controller stubs, CDP multitouch phone/tablet profiles, rotation, WebKit, OfflineAudioContext and actual bus gains. Official Hub harness tests 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% loss, authority, departures, hidden-host cancellation, time-up and shutdown. The release full remote campaign uses one client and a server-only host at baseline latency, ordinary actions and stopped client drawing; two-player 150/50/5 stress cases verify authority and lifecycle. Physical controller/touch/TV/iOS hardware, novice pacing and subjective sound quality are unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Atari original-game instructions and retrospective, reproduced 1982 manual, Howard Scott Warshaw interview, and locally rendered pack-in comic printed pages 1 and 6. Original gameplay footage was located but could not be retrieved; no claim of watching it. Linked ledger in docs/research.md separates source rules and inventions.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04 on WSL2

testingFeedback: 16 issues caught and fixed: 10 product issues and 6 test/pilot issues, itemized in docs/issues.md.
1 game-breaking issue: the engine's boot:false branch left its boot flag set and prevented browser scene changes. The imported engine is patched and regression-tested.

The ordinary-action final recovery check starting with zero cells, zero charge and a newly respawned scout; it proves the dock refill and airborne victory remain obtainable. The full remote campaign also caught pilot convergence and harness-rendering assumptions.

The first generic title screenshot: it caught layout clipping, but could not establish any siege rule or campaign completion. Semantic action traces and targeted action/boss screenshots were more useful.
engineFeedback: Native pixel primitives, hue-shifted material tones, depth-sorted actors, local lights and shared settings/audio buses made a coherent procedural visual and sound style possible without assets.

Yes. boot:false unexpectedly kept the engine in boot mode; TV-scaled modal sizing and draw-dependent resize measurements also needed investigation. Explicit scene/state assertions caught these assumptions.

The authoritative siege simulation: persistent moving cell topology, automatic bites and charge, refuge protection matrix, remote self-dangerous cannons, transforming fortress phases and exactly-once co-op rewards.
Keeping one fixed-step world independent of the native DOM shell, rendering, procedural audio and the hub clock while preserving consistent controller/touch layouts and headless testing.

One change to vendor/engine/my-3d2dge.js: clear _booting in the boot:false branch before starting hooks, so game.go works. The patch and original revision are recorded in vendor/provenance.json and vendor/engine/boot-false.patch. The session client is unmodified.
Ship a tested headless shared-world example with a host that has no avatar, serializable snapshots and a ticker independent of rendering.
promptFeedback: The concrete siege relationships, acceptance gates, exact hand-in names and insistence on an ordinary-action full playthrough made the intended finished experience clear.

PLAN.md named a different model/context configuration than TASK.md. TASK.md was used for the run metadata and artifact names. The requested novice completion time cannot be confirmed without novice playtesting.
Making remote authoritative play, recovery after a missed final shot, simultaneous rewards, controller-first menus and the single-file artifact agree across browser and headless execution.

Separate mechanically verifiable release gates from subjective pacing targets, and explicitly permit render-free remote action pilots as network simulation proof alongside separate rendered input/visual tests.

aiHub.name: Yars on the Edge
aiHub.description: Bite through living fortress shields, steal their light and call a remote siege gun that can kill its operator. Free the Ilex swarm across three escalating sectors, solo or in simultaneous co-op, and intercept the final flying heart.
aiHub.controls: Left stick/WASD move; right stick/mouse aim; R2/left click/J fire; L2/right click/Space siege then evade; Options/Escape pause; touch uses invisible twin sticks and a contextual siege button.
